q8.answer: The state, nonce, PKCE verifier, entry, next, and (for Settings only) user_id and SHA-256 sid hash are kept in the Redis record gauth:txn:{state}, with a 600 s TTL. The browser holds only the state in the gauth_txn cookie. The record is removed by GETDEL at the callback once the state checks pass, so it is single-use, or by TTL expiry. The gauth_txn cookie is cleared on every callback response.

q9.answer: The half-finished link (sub, user_id, next) is held in Redis under gauth:link:{id} with a 600 s TTL that starts at the callback. The browser refers to it only through the gauth_link cookie, which holds the id and is checked on each GET and POST of /auth/google/confirm. It is deleted on success after the DB commit, on lockout, on POST /auth/google/cancel, on a refused commit check, or when the TTL expires.

q10.answer: The permanent link is the google_identities table, with one row per link. Its sub column is the primary key, so one Google account can link to at most one user. Its user_id column is UNIQUE, so one user can have at most one Google account. These database constraints enforce both rules, and the commit and settings checks run before the insert.

q11.answer: The user is sent back to the page the flow began on (the login page or the Settings page) with the neutral message 'Google sign-in did not finish. Try again, or use email and password.' Details go only to server logs. The exchange is not retried: the txn was already consumed by GETDEL, so the authorization code cannot be reused and the user must start again.

q12.answer: The callback reads the entry field from the txn record gauth:txn:{state}, which was set at start from the entry point the user clicked. For a Settings entry, the txn also holds user_id and the SHA-256 hash of the sid. The callback hashes the current sid cookie and requires it to match that hash and to still have a live sessions row. That ties the link to the signed-in local user who started it, and the user_id comes from the txn.
